scenario: [LNUL.4.2]'s `or`, all nine cells over {true, false, null}, the dual of `and`: true wherever an operand is true, null included on the other side; false only for (false, false); null for (false, null), (null, false) and (null, null). One P fact holds t = true, f = false and n = null. Each cell `a or b` is two rules: `or_ab` fires only when the cell is true, and `or_ab_not`, `not (a or b)`, fires only when it is false, so a null cell fires neither. So the five true cells and `or_ff_not` fire, and `dead_rules_expected` requires the rest never to. A runtime answering `true or null` with null misses `or_tn` and `or_nt`. One answering `false or null` with false fires `or_fn_not`. Agenda order is source order ([LDET.5.4]). Path: each `where` is one join test over slots (nothing hoists); libds's rete/eval.c BINOP arm for DS_RETE_BINOP_OR, Mercury's ds.eval.lnul_4_2_absorbing with `true` deciding.
